supersedes: every prior figure that divided a WHOLE-STAGE row count by the eligible representative denominator
why: Four different true statements about this corpus were being quoted as one number. A whole-stage row count includes 486,955 vectors from a generation that predates the snapshot stamp; representative coverage counts DISTINCT CONTENT, not documents; and document reach is larger than representative coverage because one vector can stand for several byte-identical judgments. None of these is 'corpus coverage', and the difference between the largest and smallest of them is currently 4.6 percentage points.

generation.manifestIntegrity: VERIFIED — batches 0, 100, 235, 236, 300, 500, 765 re-hashed from disk; all seven idsHash values equal the manifest's recorded batchHashes
generation.model: BGE-M3 onnx fp32, CLS-pooled, L2-normalised, GPU sidecar
generation.stampMechanism: COLUMN DEFAULT on new1_doc_vector_stage.snapshot_hash. There is no migration and no writer in git. See generationIdentity below.

A_STAGE_PHYSICAL_ROWS.means: every vector row physically present in the stage table, of any generation
A_STAGE_PHYSICAL_ROWS.doNotUseFor: coverage of anything. This is the number that produced the inflated figures.

B_CURRENT_GENERATION_VECTOR_ROWS.means: vector rows belonging to the active embedding generation
B_CURRENT_GENERATION_VECTOR_ROWS.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM new1_doc_vector_stage WHERE snapshot_hash = '5b5d02384b46c96c'
B_CURRENT_GENERATION_VECTOR_ROWS.note: 4,179 of these are for content hashes that are NOT in the 27-Aug representative snapshot. They are post-cut deltas, not errors. That is why B is larger than the numerator of C.

C_ELIGIBLE_REPRESENTATIVE_COVERAGE.means: distinct eligible CONTENT identities that have a current-generation vector, over the frozen representative denominator
C_ELIGIBLE_REPRESENTATIVE_COVERAGE.sql: WITH cur AS (SELECT DISTINCT content_hash FROM new1_doc_vector_stage WHERE snapshot_hash = '5b5d02384b46c96c') SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.content_hash IS NOT NULL), count(*) FROM embedding_content_representative r LEFT JOIN cur c ON c.content_hash = r.content_hash

D_DOCUMENT_REACH.means: JUDGMENTS whose selected content hash is represented by a current-generation vector, over all judgments the representative snapshot admits to document-level semantic representation
D_DOCUMENT_REACH.sql: WITH cur AS (SELECT DISTINCT content_hash FROM new1_doc_vector_stage WHERE snapshot_hash = '5b5d02384b46c96c') SELECT sum(r.member_count) FILTER (WHERE c.content_hash IS NOT NULL), sum(r.member_count) FROM embedding_content_representative r LEFT JOIN cur c ON c.content_hash = r.content_hash
D_DOCUMENT_REACH.whyLargerThanC: member_count > 1 for 260,934 representatives. One common order disposing of forty writ petitions is ONE vector reaching forty judgments.
D_DOCUMENT_REACH.note: 8,420,728 is the reach denominator, NOT the corpus. judgments holds 18,758,460 rows; the rest are outside the representative snapshot's eligibility predicate entirely.

corpusContext.note: Document reach is 36.64% of what is ELIGIBLE, which is 16.4% of all judgment rows. Neither is 'the corpus is 36% embedded'.

crossLaneCorrection.diagnosis: 35.780% of 7,654,179 is 2,738,665 — a WHOLE-STAGE row count (metric A) at an earlier moment, divided by the representative denominator. It double-counts the 486,955 old-generation rows and the post-cut delta rows.
crossLaneCorrection.coincidenceWarning: That number is now numerically close to metric D (36.64%) by accident, not by derivation. Two different quantities converging for a few days is the most dangerous shape a wrong metric can take: correcting it will look like no change.
crossLaneCorrection.instruction: Do not use whole-stage row count as v2 coverage. State which of A/B/C/D you mean, every time.
crossLaneCorrection.ownership: NEW3 owns its registry. NEW1 did not edit it.
